items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to establishing the temporary advisory board on upstate transit funding; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2083

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the transportation law, in relation
to establishing the temporary advisory board on upstate transit
funding; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To improve the availability and quality of public transportation
services.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

The bill would establish a new "Upstate Transit Funding Board" within
the Department of Transportation, composed of the Commissioner and
nine other members to study, develop and make specific recommendations
for the growth, stability and sustainability of State public transit
funding options and preparing a report to the Governor and Legislature
of its findings and recommendations.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Public transportation systems all across upstate New York provide
critical transportation links between individuals and work, medical
appointments, school, shopping, and other destinations. It has been
estimated that upstate public transportation systems carry more than
570,000 riders every day, making them the equivalent of the seventh
largest transit system in the country. Transit offers riders mobility,
and is a vital component in the transportation infrastructure for
economic development, job growth, anti-poverty and housing
initiatives, energy conservation and environmental protection.

Fares alone are not sufficient to cover all the costs of providing
transit services, and as a result public transit systems must rely on
annual State funding. This bill will provide a means by which
sustainable funding options can be identified in order to provide for
growth and stability in the public transportation operating assistance
account, thus creating further opportunities for supporting mobility
options for upstate New York residents.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Unknown.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediate, to expire and be deemed repealed on the 120th day after the
Temporary Advisory Board on Upstate Transit Funding has submitted its
completed report.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No.161
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2083-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to establishing
      the  temporary  advisory  board  on  upstate  transit funding; and
      providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration there-
      of"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Transportation Law  to  create  a  Temporary
Advisory  Board  on  Upstate  Transit Funding. The 10-member Board would
study and make specific recommendations for sustainable funding  options
for  the  growth  and  stability of upstate transportation, and submit a
report to the Governor and Legislature.

  This bill suffers from the  same  concern  as  the  bill  that  I  was
constrained  to  veto last year. (Veto No. 240 of 2016). Upstate transit
funding decisions have always been, and should continue to be, addressed
in the context of the annual budget negotiations.
 
  Accordingly, in this year's State budget, the Executive and the Legis-
lature agreed  to  have  the  Department  of  Transportation  conduct  a
detailed  study  identifying  the structural issues affecting the public
transportation funding. The results of this study will be  submitted  to
myself, the Majority Leader of the Senate, and the Speaker of the Assem-
bly  later  this  year,  and  the  findings  and  recommendations can be
utilized as a basis for discussion during  next  year's  budget  negoti-
ations.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
